You are researching the Super Productivity codebase to document (A) everything the Android client does beyond the web app, and (B) all third-party integrations, plugin system and platform features.

Working dir: `W:\repos\superprod`
Source root: `W:\repos\superprod\original source code` (note the space — always quote paths)

PART A — Android / mobile:
- `android/` — read `README.md`, `README_ONLINE.md`, `README_OFFLINE.md`, `app/build.gradle`, `AndroidManifest.xml` (list ALL permissions, services, receivers, activities, intent filters, shortcuts), and the Java/Kotlin sources under `android/app/src/main/java/com/superproductivity/superproductivity/` — especially `widget/` (home screen widget: what it shows, how it updates), `service/` (foreground service? notifications?), `receiver/`, `webview/`, `crypto/`, `plugins/webdavhttp/`.
- `docs/android-home-screen-widget.md`, `docs/android-edge-to-edge-keyboard.md`
- `src/app/features/android/`, `src/app/features/mobile/`, `src/app/core/platform/`, `capacitor.config.ts`
- Find every Capacitor plugin used (package.json deps + `capacitor.config.ts` + native plugin registrations): notifications, local notifications, app lifecycle, filesystem, etc.
- Notification behavior: local reminders, scheduled notifications, foreground service, exact-alarm, what triggers them.

PART B — Integrations & extensibility:
- `src/app/features/issue/` (119 files) — enumerate EVERY issue provider (GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Gitea, OpenProject, Linear, CalDAV, Trello, ...), what each supports (import, two-way sync, polling intervals, search, create issue from task), the auth mechanism per provider (PAT? OAuth?).
- `src/app/plugins/` + `packages/plugin-api/` + `docs/plugin-development.md` — the plugin API surface: hooks, UI slots (header buttons, menu entries, side panel, dialogs), node execution, permissions.
- `src/app/features/plainspace/`, `note/`, `markdown-checklist/` briefly.
- `src/app/core/theme/`, `docs/theming-contract.md` — theming capabilities (dark mode, custom themes, CSS variables, background images/unsplash).
- `src/app/core/language/` + `src/assets/i18n/` — which languages ship (list the locale codes).
- `src/app/core-ui/shortcut/shortcut.service.ts` + `features/config/keyboard-form.const.ts` — global keyboard shortcuts list.
- `src/app/pages/search-page/` — search capabilities.
- `src/app/core/share/`, `app-uri-actions/` — deep links / share target.
- `electron/` — desktop-only features a mobile client does NOT need vs. ones users expect (tray, idle, global shortcuts, local REST API, MCP).

OUTPUT: Write a detailed markdown report to `W:\repos\superprod\.research\android-and-integrations.md` with two clear parts. Include the full permission list, the widget spec, the provider table, the plugin API surface, the locale list. Then reply with a SHORT summary (under 45 lines) covering: what Android adds over web, the exact widget/notification requirements, the integration provider list, and which desktop-only features can be skipped for a mobile+web client.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

tools.name: schedule_list

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

1: plugins {
2: 
3:     id "com.android.application"
4:     id "org.jetbrains.kotlin.android"
5: }
6: 
7: // Apply the external configuration script
8: apply from: "config.gradle"
9: 
10: // Load the application configuration properties
11: def appConfig = loadAppConfig()
12: 
13: // Retrieve the build configuration fields for Debug and Release builds
14: def debugConfigFields = getBuildConfigFields(appConfig, true)
15: def releaseConfigFields = getBuildConfigFields(appConfig, false)
16: 
17: android {
18:     defaultConfig {
19:         applicationId "com.superproductivity.superproductivity"
20:         minSdkVersion 24
21:         targetSdkVersion 36
22:         compileSdk 36
23:         versionCode 19_02_00_9000
24:         versionName "19.2.0"
25:         testInstrumentationRunner "androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner"
26:         manifestPlaceholders = [
27:                 hostName       : "app.super-productivity.com",
28:                 defaultUrl     : "https://app.super-productivity.com",
29:                 launcherName   : "Super Productivity",
30:                 assetStatements: '[{ "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], ' +
31:                         '"target": {"namespace": "web", "site": "https://app.super-productivity.com"}}]'
32:         ]
33:     }
34: 
35:     signingConfigs{
36:         release{
37:             storeFile file("../../keystore.jks")
38:             storePassword System.getenv("RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD")
39:             keyAlias System.getenv("RELEASE_KEYSTORE_ALIAS")
40:             keyPassword System.getenv("RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD")
41:         }
42:     }
43: 
44:     // Configure the build types (Debug and Release)
45:     buildTypes {
46:         debug {
47:             // Define each field in BuildConfig for the Debug build
48:             debugConfigFields.each { key, value ->
49:                 buildConfigField "String", key, value.toString()
50:             }
51:         }
52:         release {
53:             // Define each field in BuildConfig for the Release build
54:             releaseConfigFields.each { key, value ->
55:                 buildConfigField "String", key, value.toString()
56:             }
57: 
58:             signingConfig signingConfigs.release
59:             // Minification is deliberately OFF.
60:             //
61:             // Turning it on (#9766) produced a release build that crashes on
62:             // start, and it reached every Play internal-track tester before
63:             // anyone launched it: master auto-publishes to that track, so two
64:             // minified builds shipped before the crash was reported.
65:             //
66:             // At the time, nothing in CI ever started a minified build. The
67:             // emulator job installed the DEBUG variant, and the R8 job only
68:             // checked keep rules against mapping.txt — a build that dies in
69:             // onCreate passes both. That job also minified the FDROID flavor
70:             // only, while the APK that ships to Play is the PLAY flavor. That
71:             // gap is closed for play: android/run-android-checks.sh launches the
72:             // minified playR8Test APK on every Android PR. R8 full mode is the
73:             // default
74:             // under AGP 8+ (android.enableR8.fullMode is unset), so obfuscation,
75:             // shrinking, optimization and resource shrinking all ran against
76:             // this app for the first time, simultaneously, in production.
77:             //
78:             // Google Play's DEX shrinking/obfuscation requirement only starts in
79:             // February 2027, so there is nothing to buy by carrying that risk in
80:             // the meantime.
81:             //
82:             // Before re-enabling, one thing is still missing: the launch smoke
83:             // covers the PLAY flavor only. fdroidRelease would minify too, and
84:             // build-android.yml already checks both mappings on the stated
85:             // reasoning that playRelease passing says nothing about
86:             // fdroidRelease — the runtime half has to honour that as well.
87:             // shortcut: play-only launch, because nothing minified ships today;
88:             // assemble and launch fdroidR8Test in run-android-checks.sh as part
89:             // of the re-land, not after it.
90:             minifyEnabled false
91:             proguardFiles getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android.txt"), "proguard-rules.pro"
92:         }
93:         r8Test {
94:             // A permanently minified, release-configured target so R8 is exercised
95:             // in CI. Release minification was disabled after #9784; without a build
96:             // that actually runs R8, the same class of runtime-only failure returns
97:             // the moment it is re-enabled.
98:             //
99:             // This variant is NOT the instrumentation target — it is installed and
100:             // launched by android/run-android-checks.sh. Pointing `testBuildType`
101:             // here was tried and reverted: AGP then minifies the androidTest APK
102:             // with -applymapping from the app, while kotlin-stdlib and androidx.*
103:             // live in the app APK and are shrunk to what the *app* uses. Every test
104:             // died in handleBindApplication on a member the app never calls
105:             // (Intrinsics.checkNotNullParameter, then androidx.tracing.Trace), and
106:             // UTP's am_instrument_timeout of 31536000s turned each into a hang.
107:             // The keep rules to paper over that are open-ended; launching the APK
108:             // needs none of them.
109:             initWith release
110:             signingConfig signingConfigs.debug
111:             minifyEnabled true
112:             shrinkResources true
113:             setProguardFiles([
114:                     getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"),
115:                     "proguard-rules.pro",
116:             ])
117:             matchingFallbacks = ["release"]
118:         }
119:     }
120: 
121:     flavorDimensions "version"
122:     productFlavors {
123:         play {
124:             dimension "version"
125:             Properties properties = new Properties()
126:             file("google.properties").withInputStream {
127:                 properties.load(it)
128:             }
129:             buildConfigField "String", "CLIENT_ID_WEB", "\"" + properties.webToken + "\""

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI agents working in this repository. Super Productivity is a todo and time-tracking app on Angular + Electron + Capacitor.

## Repo map

Start with the [repository content map](docs/repository-map.md) (task keywords, code entry points, focused tests) and follow only the relevant links. Layer boundaries: [app map](src/app/README.md). Package ownership and checks: [packages](packages/README.md).

Read by section, not whole: the long sync docs open with a **Sections** index and `ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` with a **Decisions** index; for any long doc, `rg -n '^#{1,3} ' <file>` gives line numbers for `sed -n`. For large source files, `rg -n` first, then read the range.

## Product principles

- **Avoid feature creep:** extend existing building blocks; new UI, settings and sync surface must make users faster. A personal deep-work tool, not team management or reporting. Surface the leaner alternative when scope outgrows the problem.
- **Less noise, more depth:** no constant alerts, vanity dashboards, streaks or dopamine loops. Attention-grabbing behavior ships off by default; reminders stay opt-in.
- **Adapt, don't impose:** one calm default; add a setting only when real workflows diverge. Prefer not building a feature over adding a toggle to dodge a decision.
- **Privacy & offline first:** no analytics, tracking or telemetry; user data stays local unless explicitly synced. Core tasks and time tracking work offline; sync and integrations are optional and degrade gracefully.

## Required reading per task

- Styling → [`docs/styling-guide.md`](docs/styling-guide.md); user-facing functionality → [`docs/documentation-guide.md`](docs/documentation-guide.md)
- Sync, op-log, vector clocks → [sync index](docs/sync-and-op-log/README.md), then only the relevant contracts. Effects/reducers/bulk dispatch touching synced state → [`contributor-sync-model.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md). Judging whether a sync bug is real / how severe → [`sync-severity-triage.md`](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md)
- E2E tests → [`e2e/AGENTS.md`](e2e/AGENTS.md); marketing videos → [`e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md`](e2e/store-video/AGENTS.md)
- Load-bearing decisions → [`ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md`](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md)
- Designing a user-facing feature or writing its plan → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md) § Does it earn its place? and § Prior art
- Reviewing a feature or PR → [`docs/feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md); editing a type in `packages/plugin-api/`, `packages/shared-schema/`, `packages/sync-core/`, `src/app/op-log/core/`, or a model a `MODEL_CONFIGS` slice persists → its § Long-term cost of a change

## Core commands

**Run `npm run checkFile <file...>` on every modified `.ts` or `.scss` file before reporting work as done** (pass all files in one call). If root ESLint ignores a file (e.g. in a package), use formatting plus that package's checks in [packages/README.md](packages/README.md#validation); an ignored file is not a lint pass. Regenerate generated files through their owner script.

```bash
npm run checkFile <files...>   # prettier + lint
npm run prettier               # multi-file format
npm run lint                   # multi-file lint
npm test                       # shared packages + release tooling + Angular specs (Berlin, LA subset; CI: test:ci, full LA)
npm run test:affected          # Angular specs importing files changed vs master (Berlin + LA subset); `-- --list` to preview
npm run test:file <filepath>   # single Angular spec; package tests use package scripts
npm run test:electron          # main-process tests are electron/*.test.cjs; a .spec.ts there never runs
npm run e2e                    # browser E2E, excludes SuperSync/WebDAV
npm run e2e:file <path> -- --retries=0             # single non-sync E2E; add --grep "name"
npm run e2e:supersync:file <path> -- --retries=0   # starts and requires SuperSync
npm run e2e:webdav:file <path> -- --retries=0      # starts and requires WebDAV
npm start                      # Electron dev
npm run startFrontend          # web dev, generates environment constants first
npm run dist                   # validated Electron distribution for the host platform
```

While iterating on app code, use `npm run test:affected` instead of a full `npm test`. It covers Angular specs only: after editing `packages/*` also run that package's tests, and run `npm test` before opening a PR. It follows static imports, templates and styles; test setup, configs and unimported assets/styles trigger a full run. "Nothing to run" means nothing was tested. CI runs everything (`test:ci`).

For full provider suites prefer the [scheduled E2E workflow](.github/workflows/e2e-scheduled.yml) (`grep` filters SuperSync; `webdav_grep` + `run_webdav` for WebDAV); focused local runs and provider-switch prerequisites are in [e2e/AGENTS.md](e2e/AGENTS.md) (they need both servers and both flags, else they silently skip). Skipped tests do not validate a fix.

`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` validates nothing (root config has `files: []`); use the app/spec/Electron config or package checks ([why](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md#the-three-failure-modes-worth-remembering)).

## Project rules

- **Translations:** `T` holds keys; render with the translate pipe or `TranslateService`. Edit only `en.json`, except when adding placeholders: then update every existing translation to interpolate them. See [translation workflow](docs/TRANSLATING.md).
- **Dependencies:** never add packages to the root `dependencies`/`devDependencies`; use platform APIs, existing packages or a small in-repo implementation. A plugin may add a necessary dependency isolated to that plugin.
- **Electron:** check `IS_ELECTRON` before using Electron-specific APIs.
- **Templates & styling:** plain HTML, minimal CSS/classes, Angular Material sparingly ([styling guide](docs/styling-guide.md)). Never restyle Angular Material or shared `src/app/ui/` components for a one-off (local `.mat-*`, `.mdc-*`, `button[mat-*]` or component-internal overrides, re-declared theme styles); use existing inputs/classes/tokens/theme variables, or make the variant reusable in the shared style layer.
- **State:** never mutate NgRx state — reducers return new objects. Prefer Signals to Observables.
- **Tests:** add unit tests for new services and state logic.
- **Service size:** ≤ 1200 physical lines per `*.service.ts` (specs exempt; ESLint `max-lines`). Split by responsibility before crossing; never grow grandfathered offenders — the per-file caps pinned in `eslint.config.js` may only go down.
- **Agent-control files:** modify `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/**` or `.codex/**` only when the user explicitly asks in the current task; keep it in a dedicated commit/PR that says how it changes agent behavior. Incident-derived rules here are invariant + enforcement + issue/doc pointer only (narrative goes to `docs/`; this file must stay skimmable); date cited statistics ("measured YYYY-MM").
- **Hardening needs evidence:** grep for an observed instance before adding a guard; zero instances → record a gap instead. Allowlists only shrink (fix false positives or scope a justified disable). Verify a check can fail before trusting a pass. [Evidence](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md).
- **Does it earn its place?** Verify demand before judging implementation; decline a correct feature that adds unjustified complexity. [Review guide](docs/feature-review-guide.md).
- **Code review:** assess maintenance cost, dependencies, scale and cross-client behavior; on every change touching persisted models, the sync wire or public/plugin APIs, check them explicitly, however small. [Long-term cost](docs/feature-review-guide.md#long-term-cost-of-a-change).
- **Task component is a hot path:** `src/app/features/tasks/task/task.component.*` renders once per task in long lists; double-check every change for performance impact — no template function/getter calls, no extra change detection, no uncleaned subscriptions; verify against a large task list.

## Sync-correctness rules

These apply to all state-related work. **One user intent = one op; replayed/remote ops must not re-trigger effects.** Read [the contributor model](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md) before editing. Sync changes are high-risk: check replay determinism, concurrent/remote edits, vector-clock conflicts and data-loss modes; report material risks before marking work done.

- **Released clients:** `master` auto-publishes to Play internal, Snap `edge` and `supersync:latest`. Prove release inclusion with `git tag --contains`; an unreproduced finding is not a false one. [Severity triage](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md).
- **Reproduce first:** every sync change starts from a reproducible failure with real data shapes, not a mocked seam. A sync bug fix needs an exact E2E reproduction written first (fails without the fix, passes with it); unit tests may supplement it. Only app-unreachable server internals or providers without an E2E harness may use the narrowest real-path test instead — say why in the PR. Question unreproducible hardening rather than adding guards.

1. **Effects inject `LOCAL_ACTIONS`**, never `Actions` (`ALL_ACTIONS` only for the op-log capture effect; remote archive side effects → `ArchiveOperationHandler`). Lint: `no-actions-in-effects`. → `src/app/util/local-actions.token.ts`.
2. **Prefer action-based effects**; a selector-based effect needs `skipDuringSyncWindow()`. Lint: `require-hydration-guard`.
3. **Multi-entity change = meta-reducer**, not an effect fan-out (one reducer pass = one op). → `src/app/root-store/meta/task-shared-meta-reducers/`.
4. **Logical clock:** "what day is this?" goes through `DateService` (`getLogicalTodayDate`, `isToday`, `todayStr`). Pure reducers/selectors take `startOfNextDayDiffMs` as an arg and call `isTodayWithOffset` for replay determinism. At service boundaries use `getStartOfNextDayDiffMs()` (the raw field is `private`).
5. **`TODAY_TAG` (`'TODAY'`) is virtual** — never in `task.tagIds`; membership comes from `task.dueWithTime`/`task.dueDay`, `TODAY_TAG.taskIds` only orders. → `ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` Decision #2.
6. **Bulk dispatch loop:** needs no `setTimeout(0)` yield: capture is synchronous and writes are ordered under the op-log lock (measured 2026-10, single tab: 50–500 dispatches without yields lost no ops, #10441). Prefer one meta-reducer action (rule 3); if a follow-up depends on the loop's ops, await `OperationWriteFlushService.flushPendingWrites()` (never while holding the op-log lock). Leave existing yields in place. → [atomicity rule](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#the-atomicity-rule--one-replay-atomic-transition-one-op).
7. **`SYNC_IMPORT` / `BACKUP_IMPORT`** replace state and intentionally drop concurrent ops (CONCURRENT or LESS_THAN by vector clock) — by design, not a bug. → `SyncImportFilterService`.
8. **Vector clocks:** `MAX_VECTOR_CLOCK_SIZE = 20`; the server prunes after conflict detection, before storage. → `docs/sync-and-op-log/vector-clocks.md`.
9. **Logging:** `Log.log({ id: task.id })`, never `Log.log(task)` or a title — log history is exportable; never log user content.
10. **Don't bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` by default.** A bump does not protect released clients; new semantics must degrade gracefully (`LwwUpdatePayload` / inert markers); incompatible semantics cannot ship behind a bump alone, and compatible changes do not justify one. [Bump policy](docs/sync-and-op-log/operation-log-architecture.md#bump-policy--a-bump-does-not-protect-the-released-fleet).
11. **New persisted fields must be optional (`?`) with a runtime default** — on-disk data lacks them; don't assume a heal. If [frozen-state.spec.ts](src/app/op-log/validation/frozen-state.spec.ts) fails, fix the model, never the fixture. [Rules](docs/sync-and-op-log/persisted-model-fields.md), #9125, #9124.
12. **Conflict fixes take generic paths** (field patch, derived membership, admission sets) over per-action logic (admitting an action that meets a set's documented contract is fine; if none fits, make the smallest safe change and say why in the PR), and prove convergence and content preservation in both conflict directions with an E2E. Removing a safety stop alone is not a fix (#10264). → [conflict resolution](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#conflict-resolution--stay-on-generic-paths).
13. **No new denormalized lists or undeclared cross-entity writes** — store the fact on the child and derive membership (`ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` Decision #2). True multi-entity transitions still follow rule 3. → same section.
14. **No new crossing may reach the fail-closed stop** (`UnsupportedMultiEntityConflictError`, ending in the whole-dataset dialog). A PR adding or changing an action that declares several entity ids names its resolution path and covers it with an E2E; without one, reshape it (one declared entity, fact on the child) instead of compensating. → same section.
15. **A sync fix needs evidence of harm** — it lands only for a user report, a regression on unreleased master (revert first unless that brings back a released bug), or data loss, a sync stop or permanent content divergence on a path released clients or default settings take. Other findings from audits, reviews or fuzzing become issues with a reproduction, not PRs. → [fix intake](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#fix-intake--evidence-before-a-fix).
16. **At most five open sync PRs; each gets a fresh-context review-and-improve subagent pass before ready**: it sees only the branch, diff, tracker and [`feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md), runs the tests and fixes what makes sense; findings go fixed/not fixed in the PR body's "Review" section, not PR comments. Further work waits as a draft PR or issue. An agent session never approves its own sync PR. → [fix intake](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#fix-intake--evidence-before-a-fix).

Rules 12–16 are review-enforced.

## Anti-patterns

| Avoid                        | Do instead                               |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `any` type                   | proper types, `unknown` if truly unknown |
| Direct DOM access            | Angular bindings, `viewChild()`          |
| Side effects in constructors | `async` pipe or `toSignal`               |
| Subscribing without cleanup  | `takeUntilDestroyed()` or async pipe     |
| `NgModules` for new code     | standalone components                    |

- **Templates & styling:** plain HTML, minimal CSS/classes, Angular Material sparingly ([styling guide](docs/styling-guide.md)). Never restyle Angular Material or shared `src/app/ui/` components for a one-off (local `.mat-*`, `.mdc-*`, `button[mat-*]` or component-internal overrides, re-declared theme styles); use existing inputs/classes/tokens/theme variables, or make the variant reusable in the shared style layer.
- **State:** never mutate NgRx state — reducers return new objects. Prefer Signals to Observables.
- **Tests:** add unit tests for new services and state logic.
- **Service size:** ≤ 1200 physical lines per `*.service.ts` (specs exempt; ESLint `max-lines`). Split by responsibility before crossing; never grow grandfathered offenders — the per-file caps pinned in `eslint.config.js` may only go down.
- **Agent-control files:** modify `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/**` or `.codex/**` only when the user explicitly asks in the current task; keep it in a dedicated commit/PR that says how it changes agent behavior. Incident-derived rules here are invariant + enforcement + issue/doc pointer only (narrative goes to `docs/`; this file must stay skimmable); date cited statistics ("measured YYYY-MM").
- **Hardening needs evidence:** grep for an observed instance before adding a guard; zero instances → record a gap instead. Allowlists only shrink (fix false positives or scope a justified disable). Verify a check can fail before trusting a pass. [Evidence](docs/hardening-earns-its-place.md).
- **Does it earn its place?** Verify demand before judging implementation; decline a correct feature that adds unjustified complexity. [Review guide](docs/feature-review-guide.md).
- **Code review:** assess maintenance cost, dependencies, scale and cross-client behavior; on every change touching persisted models, the sync wire or public/plugin APIs, check them explicitly, however small. [Long-term cost](docs/feature-review-guide.md#long-term-cost-of-a-change).
- **Task component is a hot path:** `src/app/features/tasks/task/task.component.*` renders once per task in long lists; double-check every change for performance impact — no template function/getter calls, no extra change detection, no uncleaned subscriptions; verify against a large task list.

## Sync-correctness rules

These apply to all state-related work. **One user intent = one op; replayed/remote ops must not re-trigger effects.** Read [the contributor model](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md) before editing. Sync changes are high-risk: check replay determinism, concurrent/remote edits, vector-clock conflicts and data-loss modes; report material risks before marking work done.

- **Released clients:** `master` auto-publishes to Play internal, Snap `edge` and `supersync:latest`. Prove release inclusion with `git tag --contains`; an unreproduced finding is not a false one. [Severity triage](docs/sync-and-op-log/sync-severity-triage.md).
- **Reproduce first:** every sync change starts from a reproducible failure with real data shapes, not a mocked seam. A sync bug fix needs an exact E2E reproduction written first (fails without the fix, passes with it); unit tests may supplement it. Only app-unreachable server internals or providers without an E2E harness may use the narrowest real-path test instead — say why in the PR. Question unreproducible hardening rather than adding guards.

1. **Effects inject `LOCAL_ACTIONS`**, never `Actions` (`ALL_ACTIONS` only for the op-log capture effect; remote archive side effects → `ArchiveOperationHandler`). Lint: `no-actions-in-effects`. → `src/app/util/local-actions.token.ts`.
2. **Prefer action-based effects**; a selector-based effect needs `skipDuringSyncWindow()`. Lint: `require-hydration-guard`.
3. **Multi-entity change = meta-reducer**, not an effect fan-out (one reducer pass = one op). → `src/app/root-store/meta/task-shared-meta-reducers/`.
4. **Logical clock:** "what day is this?" goes through `DateService` (`getLogicalTodayDate`, `isToday`, `todayStr`). Pure reducers/selectors take `startOfNextDayDiffMs` as an arg and call `isTodayWithOffset` for replay determinism. At service boundaries use `getStartOfNextDayDiffMs()` (the raw field is `private`).
5. **`TODAY_TAG` (`'TODAY'`) is virtual** — never in `task.tagIds`; membership comes from `task.dueWithTime`/`task.dueDay`, `TODAY_TAG.taskIds` only orders. → `ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` Decision #2.
6. **Bulk dispatch loop:** needs no `setTimeout(0)` yield: capture is synchronous and writes are ordered under the op-log lock (measured 2026-10, single tab: 50–500 dispatches without yields lost no ops, #10441). Prefer one meta-reducer action (rule 3); if a follow-up depends on the loop's ops, await `OperationWriteFlushService.flushPendingWrites()` (never while holding the op-log lock). Leave existing yields in place. → [atomicity rule](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#the-atomicity-rule--one-replay-atomic-transition-one-op).
7. **`SYNC_IMPORT` / `BACKUP_IMPORT`** replace state and intentionally drop concurrent ops (CONCURRENT or LESS_THAN by vector clock) — by design, not a bug. → `SyncImportFilterService`.
8. **Vector clocks:** `MAX_VECTOR_CLOCK_SIZE = 20`; the server prunes after conflict detection, before storage. → `docs/sync-and-op-log/vector-clocks.md`.
9. **Logging:** `Log.log({ id: task.id })`, never `Log.log(task)` or a title — log history is exportable; never log user content.
10. **Don't bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` by default.** A bump does not protect released clients; new semantics must degrade gracefully (`LwwUpdatePayload` / inert markers); incompatible semantics cannot ship behind a bump alone, and compatible changes do not justify one. [Bump policy](docs/sync-and-op-log/operation-log-architecture.md#bump-policy--a-bump-does-not-protect-the-released-fleet).
11. **New persisted fields must be optional (`?`) with a runtime default** — on-disk data lacks them; don't assume a heal. If [frozen-state.spec.ts](src/app/op-log/validation/frozen-state.spec.ts) fails, fix the model, never the fixture. [Rules](docs/sync-and-op-log/persisted-model-fields.md), #9125, #9124.
12. **Conflict fixes take generic paths** (field patch, derived membership, admission sets) over per-action logic (admitting an action that meets a set's documented contract is fine; if none fits, make the smallest safe change and say why in the PR), and prove convergence and content preservation in both conflict directions with an E2E. Removing a safety stop alone is not a fix (#10264). → [conflict resolution](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#conflict-resolution--stay-on-generic-paths).
13. **No new denormalized lists or undeclared cross-entity writes** — store the fact on the child and derive membership (`ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md` Decision #2). True multi-entity transitions still follow rule 3. → same section.
14. **No new crossing may reach the fail-closed stop** (`UnsupportedMultiEntityConflictError`, ending in the whole-dataset dialog). A PR adding or changing an action that declares several entity ids names its resolution path and covers it with an E2E; without one, reshape it (one declared entity, fact on the child) instead of compensating. → same section.
15. **A sync fix needs evidence of harm** — it lands only for a user report, a regression on unreleased master (revert first unless that brings back a released bug), or data loss, a sync stop or permanent content divergence on a path released clients or default settings take. Other findings from audits, reviews or fuzzing become issues with a reproduction, not PRs. → [fix intake](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#fix-intake--evidence-before-a-fix).
16. **At most five open sync PRs; each gets a fresh-context review-and-improve subagent pass before ready**: it sees only the branch, diff, tracker and [`feature-review-guide.md`](docs/feature-review-guide.md), runs the tests and fixes what makes sense; findings go fixed/not fixed in the PR body's "Review" section, not PR comments. Further work waits as a draft PR or issue. An agent session never approves its own sync PR. → [fix intake](docs/sync-and-op-log/contributor-sync-model.md#fix-intake--evidence-before-a-fix).

Rules 12–16 are review-enforced.

## Anti-patterns

| Avoid                        | Do instead                               |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `any` type                   | proper types, `unknown` if truly unknown |
| Direct DOM access            | Angular bindings, `viewChild()`          |
| Side effects in constructors | `async` pipe or `toSignal`               |
| Subscribing without cleanup  | `takeUntilDestroyed()` or async pipe     |
| `NgModules` for new code     | standalone components                    |

1: # Online-Only Mode (Compatibility Mode) Configuration
2: 
3: **Online-Only Mode (Compatibility Mode)** allows the Super Productivity Android app to connect to the production server, a local development server, or a self-hosted server. This mode requires an internet connection and is compatible with various server setups.
4: 
5: **Note**: While Online-Only Mode offers connectivity to production, local development, or self-hosted servers, it is highly recommended to use the latest **Connectivity-Free Mode** for a more stable and reliable experience. Connectivity-Free Mode allows you to use the app without an internet connection, ensuring uninterrupted productivity, enhanced privacy, and reduced latency.
6: 
7: For more information, refer to the **[Connectivity-Free Mode Documentation (Recommended)](./README_OFFLINE.md)**.
8: 
9: If you require online features or need to connect to specific servers, proceed with the Online-Only Mode configuration below.
10: 
11: ## Setting Launch Mode to Online
12: 
13: To enable Online-Only Mode, set the `LAUNCH_MODE` to `1` or `0` in the `app_config.properties` file.
14: 
15: - **1**: Force Online-Only Mode (Compatibility Mode)
16: - **0**: Default behavior (read from SharedPreferences)
17: 
18: **Recommendation**: Set `LAUNCH_MODE` to `0` for default behavior. The app will use the default behavior, which may attempt to read from SharedPreferences and connect to online services if available.
19: 
20: ### Configuration Options
21: 
22: 1. **Launch Mode (`LAUNCH_MODE`)**
23: 
24:    ```properties
25:    LAUNCH_MODE=1
26:    ```
27: 
28:    - **0**: Default behavior (read from SharedPreferences)
29:    - **1**: Force Online-Only Mode (compatible mode)
30:    - **2**: Force Connectivity-Free Mode (for offline configuration)
31: 
32: 2. **Use Production URL**
33: 
34:    - **Condition**: Applicable when `LAUNCH_MODE` is set to `1`, or set to `0` and the user has upgraded from a previous version.
35:    - **Default**: `https://app.super-productivity.com`
36:    - **Configuration**: Ensure `ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL` is set to `false`.
37: 
38:    ```properties
39:    ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL=false
40:    ```
41: 
42: 3. **Use Local Development Server**
43: 
44:    - **Condition**: Applicable when `LAUNCH_MODE` is set to `1`, or set to `0` and the user has upgraded from a previous version.
45:    - **Configuration**: Set `ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL` to `true` and start the local server.
46: 
47:    ```properties
48:    ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL=true
49:    ```
50: 
51:    - **Start Local Server**
52: 
53:      ```bash
54:      ng serve --disable-host-check --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4200 --live-reload --watch
55:      ```
56: 
57:    - **Access URL**: `http://10.0.2.2:4200` (accessible from the Android Studio emulator and emulator's Chrome browser).
58: 
59: 4. **Use a Self-Hosted Server**
60: 
61:    - **Condition**: Applicable when `LAUNCH_MODE` is set to `1`, or set to `0` and the user has upgraded from a previous version.
62:    - **Configuration**: Set `ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL` to `false` and update `ONLINE_SERVICE_HOST` and `ONLINE_SERVICE_PROTOCOL`.
63: 
64:    ```properties
65:    ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL=false
66:    ONLINE_SERVICE_HOST=your.server.address
67:    ONLINE_SERVICE_PROTOCOL=https
68:    ```
69: 
70: ## How to Modify the URL
71: 
72: You can edit the URL that the web view loads by modifying the `app_config.properties` file located in the project's root directory. This allows you to easily switch between a production server, a local development server, or a self-hosted server.
73: 
74: ### Relevant Settings
75: 
76: - **`LAUNCH_MODE`**:
77: 
78:   - `0`: Default behavior (read from SharedPreferences)
79:   - `1`: Force Online-Only Mode
80:   - `2`: Force Connectivity-Free Mode
81: 
82: - **When `LAUNCH_MODE` is `1` or `0` (with upgrade)**:
83:   - **`ONLINE_SERVICE_IS_LOCAL`**:
84:     - `true`: Load from local development server (`http://10.0.2.2:4200`).
85:     - `false`: Load from production or self-hosted server.
86:   - **`ONLINE_SERVICE_HOST`**:
87:     - Defines the server's address.
88:   - **`ONLINE_SERVICE_PROTOCOL`**:
89:     - `http` or `https`.
90: 
91: ## Important Notes
92: 
93: - **Local Modifications**: The `app_config.properties` file is intended for local modifications only. **DO NOT COMMIT** this file unless you are absolutely sure of the changes.
94: - **Switching Servers**: By configuring these properties, you can seamlessly switch between default, online, and offline launch behaviors without making direct changes to your Kotlin source files, improving your development workflow and offering flexibility in deployment.

(End of file - total 94 lines)
</content>

9: For users performing a **new installation**, setting `LAUNCH_MODE` to `2` ensures that the app starts in Connectivity-Free Mode by default. This avoids any attempts to connect to online services, providing a seamless offline experience from the outset.
10:

12: 
13: ## Building and Running super-productivity-android Locally
14: 
15: ### 1. Clone the Repository
16: 
17: To set up the project, clone the `super-productivity` repository instead of directly cloning the `super-productivity-android` repository. This ensures that all submodules, including the Android project, are properly initialized.
18: 
19: ```bash
20: git clone https://github.com/super-productivity/super-productivity.git
21: cd super-productivity
22: git submodule init
23: git submodule update
24: ```
25:

27:

29: 
30: ```bash
31: npm install
32: ```
33:

37: 
38: - **For Testing Builds:**
39: 
40:   ```bash
41:   npm run dist:android
42:   ```
43: 
44: - **For Production Builds:**
45: 
46:   ```bash
47:   npm run dist:android:prod
48:   ```
49:

51: 
52: You can install the compiled Android application using either Android Studio or npm scripts.
53:

55:

67:     ```
68:

72:     npm run install:android:prod
73:     ```

78: - **No Additional Configuration**: Connectivity-Free Mode does not require further configuration beyond setting the `LAUNCH_MODE` to `0` or `2`.

18: private class TaskListRemoteViewsFactory(

24:     override fun onCreate() {}
25: 
26:     override fun onDataSetChanged() {
27:         tasks = try {
28:             val json = (context.applicationContext as App).keyValStore
29:                 .get(WidgetData.KEYVAL_KEY, "{}")
30:             WidgetData.parse(json, WidgetDoneQueue.peek(context)).take(MAX_TASKS)
31:         } catch (e: Exception) {
32:             Log.e(TAG, "Failed to parse widget data", e)
33:             emptyList()

44:         val rv = RemoteViews(context.packageName, R.layout.widget_task_row)
45: 
46:         if (position >= tasks.size) {

48:         }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LinearLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent"
    android:orientation="vertical"
    android:background="@drawable/widget_bg"
    android:paddingStart="10dp"
    android:paddingEnd="10dp"
    android:paddingTop="12dp"
    android:paddingBottom="6dp">

    <LinearLayout
        android:id="@+id/widget_header"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:orientation="horizontal"
        android:gravity="center_vertical"
        android:paddingStart="6dp"
        android:paddingEnd="6dp"
        android:paddingBottom="10dp">

        <ImageView
            android:layout_width="18dp"
            android:layout_height="18dp"
            android:src="@drawable/ic_stat_sp"
            android:tint="@color/widget_brand"
            android:contentDescription="" />

        <TextView
            android:id="@+id/widget_header_title"
            android:layout_width="0dp"
            android:layout_height="wrap_content"
            android:layout_weight="1"
            android:layout_marginStart="8dp"
            android:text="@string/widget_header_title"
            android:textColor="@color/widget_ink"
            android:textSize="16sp"
            android:textStyle="bold" />
    </LinearLayout>

    <!-- FrameLayout, not View: plain View is not on the RemoteViews whitelist -->
    <FrameLayout
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="1dp"
        android:background="@color/widget_separator" />

    <ListView
        android:id="@+id/widget_task_list"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="0dp"
        android:layout_weight="1"
        android:divider="@null"
        android:dividerHeight="0dp"
        android:scrollbars="none" />

    <TextView
        android:id="@+id/widget_empty"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="match_parent"
        android:text="@string/widget_empty"
        android:textColor="@color/widget_ink_muted"
        android:textSize="14sp"
        android:gravity="center"
        android:visibility="gone" />

</LinearLayout>

=== ROW ===
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LinearLayout xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:id="@+id/widget_task_row"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="wrap_content"
    android:orientation="horizontal"
    android:gravity="center_vertical"
    android:paddingStart="6dp"
    android:paddingEnd="0dp"
    android:minHeight="34dp">

    <ImageView
        android:id="@+id/widget_project_dot"
        android:layout_width="8dp"
        android:layout_height="8dp"
        android:layout_marginEnd="10dp"
        android:src="@drawable/widget_project_dot"
        android:contentDescription="" />

    <TextView
        android:id="@+id/widget_task_title"
        android:layout_width="0dp"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_weight="1"
        android:textColor="@color/widget_ink"
        android:textSize="15sp"
        android:maxLines="2"
        android:ellipsize="end" />

    <ImageView
        android:id="@+id/widget_done_checkbox"
        android:layout_width="38dp"
        android:layout_height="34dp"
        android:paddingStart="9dp"
        android:paddingEnd="9dp"
        android:paddingTop="7dp"
        android:paddingBottom="7dp"
        android:layout_marginStart="4dp"
        android:src="@drawable/ic_widget_check_outline"
        android:scaleType="fitCenter"
        android:contentDescription="@string/widget_task_done" />

</LinearLayout>

=== SHORTCUTS ===
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Launcher shortcuts (long-press the app icon), mirroring the iOS Home Screen
  quick actions in ios/App/App/Info.plist. Each one opens a
  com.super-productivity.app://<host> URL that parse-app-uri-quick-action.ts
  handles; tools/verify-android-shortcuts.test.js checks the hosts, targets and
  labels against the parser, the manifest and strings.xml.

  They go through AppShortcutActivity rather than CapacitorMainActivity because
  static shortcuts are always launched with FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK — see the
  comment on that class. targetPackage can't be a placeholder here; it is the
  applicationId, which no build variant changes.
-->
<shortcuts xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
  <shortcut
    android:shortcutId="add-task"
    android:enabled="true"
    android:icon="@drawable/ic_shortcut_add_task"
    android:shortcutShortLabel="@string/shortcut_add_task">
    <intent
      android:action="android.intent.action.VIEW"
      android:data="com.super-productivity.app://add-task"
      android:targetClass="com.superproductivity.superproductivity.AppShortcutActivity"
      android:targetPackage="com.superproductivity.superproductivity" />
  </shortcut>
  <shortcut
    android:shortcutId="today"
    android:enabled="true"
    android:icon="@drawable/ic_shortcut_today"
    android:shortcutShortLabel="@string/shortcut_today">
    <intent
      android:action="android.intent.action.VIEW"
      android:data="com.super-productivity.app://today"
      android:targetClass="com.superproductivity.superproductivity.AppShortcutActivity"
      android:targetPackage="com.superproductivity.superproductivity" />
  </shortcut>
  <shortcut
    android:shortcutId="inbox"
    android:enabled="true"
    android:icon="@drawable/ic_shortcut_inbox"
    android:shortcutShortLabel="@string/shortcut_inbox">
    <intent
      android:action="android.intent.action.VIEW"
      android:data="com.super-productivity.app://inbox"
      android:targetClass="com.superproductivity.superproductivity.AppShortcutActivity"
      android:targetPackage="com.superproductivity.superproductivity" />
  </shortcut>
</shortcuts>

1: package com.superproductivity.superproductivity.service
2: 
3: import android.app.Service
4: import android.content.Context
5: import android.content.Intent
6: import android.os.IBinder
7: import android.util.Log
8: import androidx.core.app.NotificationManagerCompat
9: 
10: /** What getTrackingElapsed() hands the JS recovery. */
11: data class BridgeSnapshot(val taskId: String, val elapsedMs: Long, val resume: Boolean)
12: 
13: class TrackingForegroundService : Service() {
14: 
15:     companion object {
16:         const val TAG = "TrackingService"
17: 
18:         const val ACTION_START = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_START_TRACKING"
19:         const val ACTION_STOP = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_STOP_TRACKING"
20:         const val ACTION_UPDATE = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_UPDATE_TRACKING"
21:         const val ACTION_PAUSE = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_PAUSE_TRACKING"
22:         const val ACTION_DONE = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_MARK_DONE"
23:         const val ACTION_GET_ELAPSED = "com.superproductivity.ACTION_GET_ELAPSED"
24: 
25:         const val EXTRA_TASK_ID = "task_id"
26:         const val EXTRA_TASK_TITLE = "task_title"
27:         const val EXTRA_TIME_SPENT = "time_spent_ms"
28: 
29:         // Static state accessible from JavaScriptInterface. Mirrored to
30:         // TrackingStateStore on every change so a process kill does not lose
31:         // the session (#7390); restoreIfIdle() reads it back in a new process.
32:         @Volatile
33:         internal var taskTitle: String = ""
34:             private set
35: 
36:         @Volatile
37:         var currentTaskId: String? = null
38:             private set
39: 
40:         @Volatile
41:         var startTimestamp: Long = 0
42:             private set
43: 
44:         @Volatile
45:         var accumulatedMs: Long = 0
46:             private set
47: 
48:         @Volatile
49:         var isTracking: Boolean = false
50:             private set
51: 
52:         // False only for a session restored after a user-requested exit: the
53:         // JS recovery credits it, then stops tracking instead of resuming.
54:         @Volatile
55:         var resumeAfterRestore: Boolean = true
56:             private set
57: 
58:         // Marks the window between startForegroundService() and the first
59:         // startForeground() inside onStartCommand(). A stop arriving in that
60:         // window must NOT use stopService() — tearing down a start-foreground
61:         // service before it promotes crashes the process with
62:         // ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException (AOSP bringDownServiceLocked,
63:         // fired while fgRequired is still true). JavaScriptInterface reads this to
64:         // route such stops through onStartCommand (ACTION_STOP) instead.
65:         @Volatile
66:         var isStartPending: Boolean = false
67:             private set
68: 
69:         fun markStartPending() {
70:             isStartPending = true
71:         }
72: 
73:         fun clearStartPending() {
74:             isStartPending = false
75:         }
76: 
77:         fun getElapsedMs(): Long {
78:             return if (isTracking && startTimestamp > 0) {
79:                 (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTimestamp) + accumulatedMs
80:             } else {
81:                 accumulatedMs
82:             }
83:         }
84: 
85:         // The state helpers below share the companion lock so a bridge-thread
86:         // restoreIfIdle() cannot re-load a session that a main-thread stop is
87:         // in the middle of clearing.
88: 
89:         @Synchronized
90:         internal fun setState(context: Context, state: TrackingState) {
91:             TrackingStateStore.save(context, state)
92:             applyInMemory(state)
93:             resumeAfterRestore = true
94:         }
95: 
96:         @Synchronized
97:         fun clearState(context: Context) {
98:             isTracking = false
99:             currentTaskId = null
100:             startTimestamp = 0
101:             accumulatedMs = 0
102:             taskTitle = ""
103:             resumeAfterRestore = true
104:             TrackingStateStore.clear(context)
105:         }
106: 
107:         /**
108:          * After a process kill the companion starts empty while the persisted
109:          * session is still on disk (every stop clears both, so this only happens
110:          * in a new process). Load it back, with the total frozen at the old
111:          * process's death, so getTrackingElapsed() hands the JS cold-start
112:          * recovery the time tracked until the kill. The in-memory state wins
113:          * whenever it is live, so this never re-anchors a running session.
114:          * After a deliberate user stop (API 34+ only) the session is marked
115:          * not to resume; below that the reason is unknown or ambiguous and it
116:          * always resumes. [exits] is a seam for tests: real exit records can't
117:          * be faked on a device.
118:          */
119:         @Synchronized
120:         fun restoreIfIdle(
121:             context: Context,
122:             exits: (Context) -> List<ProcessExit> = TrackingStateStore::anchorProcessExits
123:         ) {
124:             if (isTracking) return
125:             val persisted = TrackingStateStore.load(context) ?: return
126:             val exit = TrackingState.pickExit(exits(context), persisted.startTimestamp)
127:             val state = persisted.frozenAtExit(exit?.timestamp, System.currentTimeMillis())
128:             val resume = TrackingState.shouldResumeAfter(exit)
129:             Log.d(
130:                 TAG,
131:                 "Restoring persisted tracking state: taskId=${state.taskId}, " +
132:                     "exitKnown=${exit != null}, resume=$resume"
133:             )
134:             if (resume) {
135:                 // Persist the re-anchored state too, so a second kill before JS
136:                 // re-anchors is measured from here rather than the old anchor.
137:                 setState(context, state)
138:             } else {
139:                 // Frozen (no anchor) so a late bridge read never credits time
140:                 // after the stop. The old record stays on disk, so a kill before
141:                 // JS stops this re-derives the same total.
142:                 applyInMemory(state.copy(startTimestamp = 0))
143:                 resumeAfterRestore = false
144:             }
145:         }
146: 
147:         /**
148:          * The active session for the JS bridge, restoring a persisted one
149:          * first, or null when nothing is tracked. Read under the companion
150:          * lock so a main-thread start/update/stop cannot interleave and pair
151:          * one task's id with another task's total.
152:          */
153:         @Synchronized
154:         fun snapshotForBridge(context: Context): BridgeSnapshot? {
155:             restoreIfIdle(context)
156:             val taskId = currentTaskId
157:             return if (isTracking && taskId != null) {
158:                 BridgeSnapshot(taskId, getElapsedMs(), resumeAfterRestore)
159:             } else {
160:                 null
161:             }
162:         }
163: 
164:         private fun applyInMemory(state: TrackingState) {
165:             currentTaskId = state.taskId
166:             taskTitle = state.taskTitle
167:             // Anchor first, accumulated second: a torn getElapsedMs() read from
168:             // the JS bridge thread then under-reports (caught by the
169:             // negative-duration keep-app-value path) instead of double-counting
170:             // the since-last-anchor gap — which can be hours now that nothing
171:             // re-anchors every second.
172:             startTimestamp = state.startTimestamp
173:             accumulatedMs = state.accumulatedMs
174:             isTracking = true
175:         }
176:     }
177: 
178:     override fun onCreate() {
179:         super.onCreate()
180:         Log.d(TAG, "Service created")
181:         TrackingNotificationHelper.createChannel(this)
182:     }
183: 
184:     override fun onStartCommand(intent: Intent?, flags: Int, startId: Int): Int {
185:         Log.d(TAG, "onStartCommand: action=${intent?.action}")
186:         // A fresh process (after a kill) has an empty companion: reload the
187:         // persisted session so ACTION_UPDATE/STOP act on it and the
188:         // notification shows the task again.
189:         restoreIfIdle(this)
190: 
191:         // Android documents successful startForeground() as the safe path
192:         // after startForegroundService(). Promote before handling actions so
193:         // newly started services satisfy that contract.
194:         if (!ensureForegroundNotification()) {
195:             clearStartPending()
196:             reportForegroundFailure()
197:             stopAfterForegroundFailure(startId)
198:             return START_NOT_STICKY
199:         }
200:         clearStartPending()
201: 
202:         when (intent?.action) {
203:             ACTION_START -> {
204:                 val taskId = intent.getStringExtra(EXTRA_TASK_ID)
205:                 if (taskId == null) {
206:                     Log.w(TAG, "ACTION_START without taskId")
207:                     if (!isTracking) {
208:                         stopForegroundAndSelf()
209:                     }
210:                     return START_NOT_STICKY
211:                 }
212:                 val title = intent.getStringExtra(EXTRA_TASK_TITLE) ?: "Task"
213:                 val timeSpentMs = intent.getLongExtra(EXTRA_TIME_SPENT, 0L)
214: 
215:                 if (!startTracking(taskId, title, timeSpentMs)) {
216:                     reportForegroundFailure()
217:                     stopAfterForegroundFailure(startId)
218:                     return START_NOT_STICKY
219:                 }
220:             }
221: 
222:             ACTION_UPDATE -> {
223:                 if (!isTracking) {
224:                     Log.d(TAG, "Ignoring ACTION_UPDATE - service not tracking")
225:                     stopForegroundAndSelf()
226:                     return START_NOT_STICKY
227:                 }
228:                 val timeSpentMs = intent.getLongExtra(EXTRA_TIME_SPENT, accumulatedMs)
229:                 updateTimeSpent(timeSpentMs)
230:             }
231: 
232:             ACTION_STOP -> {
233:                 if (isTracking) {
234:                     stopTracking()
235:                 } else {
236:                     Log.d(TAG, "Ignoring STOP action - service not tracking")
237:                     stopForegroundAndSelf()
238:                 }
239:             }
240: 
241:             else -> {
242:                 Log.d(TAG, "Service started without action, stopping")
243:                 stopForegroundAndSelf()
244:             }
245:         }
246: 
247:         return START_NOT_STICKY
248:     }
249: 
250:     private fun ensureForegroundNotification(): Boolean {
251:         val notification = try {
252:             if (isTracking && taskTitle.isNotEmpty()) {
253:                 TrackingNotificationHelper.buildNotification(
254:                     this,
255:                     taskTitle,
256:                     getElapsedMs()
257:                 )

135:     override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
136:         // Register plugins before calling super.onCreate()
137:         registerPlugin(SafBridgePlugin::class.java)
138:         registerPlugin(WebDavHttpPlugin::class.java)
139:         registerPlugin(NavigationBarPlugin::class.java)
140: 
141:         // On Activity recreation (config change / process death) getIntent() still
142:         // holds the original launch intent and BridgeActivity.load() replays it
143:         // through onNewIntent — without the LAUNCHED_FROM_HISTORY flag, so the
144:         // recents guard in onNewIntent doesn't catch it. A stale VIEW data URI
145:         // would re-fire appUrlOpen and duplicate the URL scheme task action;
146:         // clear it (mirrors the savedInstanceState guard for share intents below).
147:         if (savedInstanceState != null) {
148:             intent?.data = null
149:         }
150:         try {
151:             super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
152:         } catch (e: Throwable) {
153:             showWebViewInitFailureOrThrow("BridgeActivity.onCreate() failed to initialize WebView", e)
154:             return
155:         }
156:         // A recovery relaunch was scheduled during super.onCreate()/load(); don't
157:         // fall through to the (now-doomed) bridge.webView null check and re-handle it.
158:         if (webViewBlocked || webViewRecoveryScheduled) {
159:             return
160:         }
161: 
162:         val webView = bridge?.webView
163:         if (webView == null) {
164:             showWebViewInitFailure("Bridge or WebView is null after onCreate")
165:             return
166:         }
167: 
168:         try {
169:             printWebViewVersion(webView)
170: 
171:             // DEBUG ONLY
172:             if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) {
173:                 Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).postDelayed({
174:                     val debugToast = Toast.makeText(this, "DEBUG", Toast.LENGTH_SHORT)
175:                     debugToast.show()
176:                     Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).postDelayed({ debugToast.cancel() }, 100)
177:                 }, 10_000)
178:                 WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)
179:             }
180: 
181:             webViewCompatibility?.let {
182:                 if (it.status == WebViewCompatibilityChecker.Status.WARN) {
183:                     Log.w(
184:                         "SP-WebView",
185:                         "WebView version ${it.majorVersion ?: "unknown"} below recommended ${WebViewCompatibilityChecker.RECOMMENDED_CHROMIUM_VERSION}",
186:                     )
187:                 }
188:             }
189: 
190:             // Hide the action bar
191:             supportActionBar?.hide()
192: 
193:             // Initialize JavaScriptInterface
194:             javaScriptInterface = JavaScriptInterface(this, webView)
195: 
196:             // Initialize WebView
197:             WebHelper().setupView(webView, false)
198: 
199:             // Inject JavaScriptInterface into Capacitor's WebView
200:             webView.addJavascriptInterface(
201:                 javaScriptInterface,
202:                 WINDOW_INTERFACE_PROPERTY
203:             )
204:             if (BuildConfig.FLAVOR.equals("fdroid")) {
205:                 webView.addJavascriptInterface(
206:                     javaScriptInterface,
207:                     WINDOW_PROPERTY_F_DROID
208:                 )
209:             }
210:         } catch (e: Throwable) {
211:             showWebViewInitFailureOrThrow("WebView setup failed", e)
212:             return
213:         }
214: 
215:         // We made it past the pre-flight version check and the WebView setup.
216:         // Persist the detected version so a transient mis-read on a later launch
217:         // can't lock the user out, and clear any prior user override if healthy.
218:         WebViewCompatibilityChecker.recordSuccessfulLoad(this, webViewCompatibility?.majorVersion)
219: 
220: 
221:         // Remember the WebView's resting layout height (e.g. MATCH_PARENT) so the
222:         // keyboard workaround can restore it on hide. See
223:         // adjustWebViewHeightForKeyboard.
224:         webViewLayoutHeightDefault = bridge?.webView?.layoutParams?.height
225: 
226:         // Handle keyboard visibility changes
227:         val rootView = findViewById<View>(android.R.id.content)
228:         rootView.viewTreeObserver.addOnGlobalLayoutListener {
229:             val rect = Rect()
230:             rootView.getWindowVisibleDisplayFrame(rect)
231:             val screenHeight = rootView.rootView.height
232: 
233:             val keypadHeight = screenHeight - rect.bottom
234:             val isKeyboardOpen = keypadHeight > screenHeight * 0.15
235:             callJSInterfaceFunctionIfExists(
236:                 "next",
237:                 "isKeyboardShown$",
238:                 if (isKeyboardOpen) "true" else "false"
239:             )
240:             adjustWebViewHeightForKeyboard(rect, isKeyboardOpen)
241:             pushStatusBarOverlap(rect)
242:             // After the shim, so the log shows the height it applied. See
243:             // logImeGeometryOnTransition.
244:             logImeGeometryOnTransition(rect, isKeyboardOpen)
245:         }
246: 
247:         // Register broadcast receiver for focus mode timer completion
248:         LocalBroadcastManager.getInstance(this).registerReceiver(
249:             timerCompleteReceiver,
250:             IntentFilter(FocusModeForegroundService.ACTION_TIMER_COMPLETE)
251:         )
252:         isTimerCompleteReceiverRegistered = true
253:         LocalBroadcastManager.getInstance(this).registerReceiver(
254:             foregroundServiceFailureReceiver,
255:             IntentFilter(ForegroundServiceFailure.ACTION)
256:         )
257:         isForegroundServiceFailureReceiverRegistered = true
258:         LocalBroadcastManager.getInstance(this).registerReceiver(
259:             widgetDoneDrainReceiver,
260:             IntentFilter(TaskListWidgetProvider.ACTION_WIDGET_DONE_DRAIN)
261:         )
262:         isWidgetDoneDrainReceiverRegistered = true
263: 
264:         // Schedule background sync worker if credentials are configured
265:         if (BackgroundSyncCredentialStore.get(this) != null) {
266:             SyncReminderScheduler.ensureScheduled(this)
267:         }

269:         // Handle initial intent (cold start) only on a fresh launch.
270:         // On Activity recreation (config change) savedInstanceState is non-null
271:         // and getIntent() still holds the original share/reminder Intent — re-running
272:         // handleIntent() there would create a duplicate task from the same share.
273:         if (savedInstanceState == null) {
274:             handleIntent(intent)
275:         }
276:     }
